correctness.rationale: The source's regularized equation F(q,rho)=0 has F(kappa,0)=0 and F_q(kappa,0)=Si(pi)>0. The defining integrals C0 and S0 have the required first two parameter derivatives at (0,pi), because the sine/cosine numerators cancel the t^{-1} endpoint singularity even after logarithmic differentiation. Implicit differentiation gives F_rho(kappa,0)=kappa^2 A-pi kappa B and hence q'(0)=kappa^2(SB-A)/S. Multiplying the C2 expansion of q by rho gives nu(rho)=kappa rho+beta rho^2+O(rho^3).

value.rationale: The fresh proof explicitly introduces q(rho)=nu(rho)/rho as the normalized small-parameter quantity and builds a dedicated root-ratio certificate around it. Determining q'(0) gives the first sensitivity invariant beyond the source's limiting constant and quantifies the initial departure of the optimal parameter curve. This is a natural endpoint refinement of a structural parameter central to the all-rho theorem, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
